agentContributions.notes: Defect: formatStops loop bound i < stops.length - 1 skips the last stop. The fix site is the loop bound in formatStops. Verification criteria are black-box checks on the string formatStops returns.

Read src/schedule.ts and test/schedule.test.ts to ground refinements in actual code. Key findings: (1) The bug is i < stops.length - 1 in formatStops, which omits the last stop entirely — both name and minutes. (2) Each stop is formatted as 'Name (Xm)' with minutes — this per-stop format must survive the fix, so AC5 was added as a regression guard. (3) The existing test only checks for the arrow and first stop name, never the last stop — confirming the bug is real and untested. (4) A single-stop line is an edge case the fix must handle (no separator needed). (5) Openspec's AC1 was refined to Given/When/Then and made explicit about 'N stop names' for precise testability. (6) Openspec's AC2 was refined to specify no leading/trailing separator (the bug fix could introduce a trailing separator if done naively). (7) Openspec's AC3 was refined to state the expected output (empty string) rather than the vague 'renders without error'.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes:
Both agents added meaningful, non-overlapping value. OpenSpec identified the root cause (loop bound `i < stops.length - 1` in formatStops skips the final stop) and framed verification as black-box string checks. SpecKit grounded the analysis in actual source code, adding depth OpenSpec lacked: the per-stop `Name (Xm)` format must survive the fix (regression guard), the existing test never asserts the final stop (confirming the bug is real and untested), the single-stop edge case, and refinement of vague ACs toward Given/When/Then testability. No redundancy between the two.

Manifest evidence confirmed both declared paths (src/schedule.ts, test/schedule.test.ts) exist. I independently read both files and every code-level claim in the spec is accurate: `formatStops` has exactly `for (let i = 0; i < stops.length - 1; i++)`, the per-stop template is `${stops[i].name} (${stops[i].minutes}m)`, the separator is `' -> '`, and `totalMinutes` reads `stops[stops.length - 1].minutes` directly (independent of the bug). The test file's `LINE` constant holds Union/Bloor/Eglinton, and existing tests assert only `'->'` and `'Union'` — never `'Eglinton'` or `'Bloor'`, never the full expected string, never `formatStops([])`. The prescribed test additions are valid and reuse the existing LINE constant and formatStops import.

Verification criteria are fully observable: specific stop names (Union, Bloor, Eglinton), the arrow separator, and empty-string-for-empty-input. The fix prescription is surgical — one loop-bound change, no string-construction changes needed.

Plan alignment: aligned:true is correct. The detectivePlan investigated formatStops loop bound, totalMinutes independence, and test gaps; the final fixSiteAnalysis addresses the first two with changes and correctly omits totalMinutes (no change needed). No unexplained pivot — the plan and final answer share the same symbols and consistent reasoning.

The acceptanceChanged:false with notes describing AC refinement is the expected brownfield redaction behavior — not flagged. The guardVocabulary is well-constructed: blacklists internal mechanism terms and whitelists user-facing surface terms.
